question: GQ-001
subject: my own pre-push hook refused a push, and it was right
what_happened: push rejected; I first read it as a transient remote error and printed "pushed" — the tail -1 in my command had HIDDEN the refusal line
lesson_about_my_own_reporting: a pipeline ending in tail can drop the very line that says the operation failed; PUSH REFUSED was there and I did not see it

the_real_cause.meaning: exit 8 is INCOMPLETE — the index held 1,328 books while the fetch I had just run put 1,528 texts on disk. --check was CORRECT.

the_defect_in_the_TEST.what: the case asserted rc==0 AND before==after, but its name claims only the second
the_defect_in_the_TEST.why_wrong: rc==0 asserts the corpus is currently up to date — a fact about the WORLD, not about --check, and false during any fetch
the_defect_in_the_TEST.consequence: the suite would fail on every ingest, training me to ignore it — the exact failure mode I spent today fixing

the_fix: accept rc 0 (up to date) and rc 8 (INCOMPLETE, correctly reported); reject anything else, and mutation always
